title: One Open Reconstruction Contract per Loss Address, and Claim Proceeds Shared with Mitigation Jobs
content:
**1. One open contract.** No other Reconstruction contract of the same customer for the same loss address may be open when a new contract is proposed. A contract is open in every status except closed and cancelled; for multifamily units the unit number is part of the address, so each unit carries its own contract.

**2. Proceeds shared with the mitigation jobs.** The rebuild contract shares the claim file's dwelling-coverage payments with the mitigation jobs of the same loss: under the claim payment allocation rule of the Insurance Claim Services charter, mitigation jobs are paid first and the rebuild contract last, so insurance proceeds reach the rebuild only after every mitigation job of the claim file has been paid in full.

## How clause 1 is judged

- **When**: at the moment a new Reconstruction contract is proposed.
- **Evidence**: the company's own contract records, not the customer's account of them.
- **Same object**: a contract counts against the new proposal only when it is held by the same customer and carries the same loss address.
- **Open statuses**: proposed, signed, permitted, in construction, substantially complete and final invoiced. A closed or cancelled contract is not open.

| Existing contract of the same customer at the same loss address | New proposal at that address |
|---|---|
| None | May be proposed |
| One in proposed, signed, permitted, in construction, substantially complete or final invoiced status | May not be proposed |
| Only closed or cancelled ones | May be proposed |

## Cases (hypothetical)

- An owner whose earlier contract at the same street address was cancelled may be proposed a new contract there; a cancelled contract is not open.
- An association holding a final-invoiced contract for unit 4 of a building may not be proposed a second contract for unit 4 while that contract is open, but may be proposed one for unit 7, because the unit number is part of the address.
